# Policy Rules Checklist: Expense Policy Validator

**Purpose**: Review whether policy-rule requirements are complete, precise, and unambiguous
**Created**: 2026-09-22
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Policy Value Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are all policy-controlled monetary values identified with an explicit currency and unit, including per diem caps, receipt thresholds, exchange rates, and reported amounts? [Completeness, Spec §FR-003, §FR-004, §FR-006, §FR-010, §FR-011]
- [ ] CHK002 Is the unit and interpretation of each non-monetary policy value explicit, including reporting precision, partial-day multipliers, travel-day context, and city-tier identifiers? [Clarity, Spec §FR-003, §FR-010, §FR-011]
- [ ] CHK003 Does the specification define a stated limit or threshold for every policy rule that constrains an expense, rather than referring only to a generic cap or requirement? [Completeness, Spec §FR-003, §FR-004, §FR-010]
- [ ] CHK004 Are the policy data fields that carry each cap, threshold, rate, currency, and precision value clearly identified as authoritative and changeable data? [Traceability, Spec §FR-010, Assumptions]

## Boundary and Rule Semantics

- [ ] CHK005 Does the specification explicitly state whether an expense exactly equal to each applicable per diem cap is compliant? [Clarity, Spec §FR-003, User Story 1 Scenario 3]
- [ ] CHK006 Does the specification explicitly state whether an expense exactly equal to the receipt threshold requires a receipt? [Gap, Boundary Case, Spec §FR-004]
- [ ] CHK007 Are the comparison directions for caps, thresholds, and receipt requirements unambiguous, including the meaning of below, above, equal to, and missing? [Clarity, Spec §FR-003, §FR-004, Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK008 Are partial-day or travel-context adjustments defined with their applicability, unit, and exact boundary behavior before a cap comparison is made? [Completeness, Spec §FR-003, Key Entities]
- [ ] CHK009 Does the specification define how multiple applicable policy rules interact when a line has both a spending cap and a receipt requirement? [Coverage, Spec §FR-002, §FR-003, §FR-004]

## Currency Handling

- [ ] CHK010 Does the specification identify the policy currency and state which direction each supplied exchange rate applies, including how a foreign amount becomes comparable to a policy-currency cap? [Clarity, Spec §FR-005, §FR-006, Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK011 Does the specification define which rate applies when a submission contains euros or pounds, including the rate's effective scope for the validation run? [Completeness, Spec §FR-006, User Story 3]
- [ ] CHK012 Does the specification state the exact outcome when a required exchange rate is missing, malformed, unsupported, or ambiguous, including whether the affected line is an error rather than an assumed conversion? [Exception Flow, Spec §FR-006, §FR-008, Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK013 Are currency conversion, cap comparison, and reporting precision requirements consistent about when exact values are preserved and when half-up rounding is applied? [Consistency, Spec §FR-006, §FR-011, Edge Cases]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation.
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state but must not modify markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`.
- Add comments or findings inline when a policy requirement needs revision.
